name: Presentation API
plain: Lets a page show itself on a second screen such as a Chromecast.
meaning: Sees which nearby display receivers exist only after the person picks one; lets a page cast to TVs.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets a page show itself on a second screen such as a Chromecast.

limits.headline: Can show itself on a second screen you choose, like a Chromecast
limits.user_action: You tap Cast and pick a screen from the list.
can: List nearby screens you can show the page on
Show a page or video on the screen you pick
Send messages to the second screen while it runs
cannot: Pick a screen without you choosing
Cast on Firefox, Safari or iPhone
See other devices on your network beyond the list
Cast after you close the page
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge support it. Firefox and Safari, including iPhone, do not.

story.what_it_is: A page can send itself to a second screen, like a Chromecast.

marketing.name: Presentation API
marketing.pitch: MDN says it lets a page show content on a second screen like a TV or projector.

story.for_you: You tap a Cast button, pick a screen from a list and the page shows up on the TV. Your phone becomes the remote.
story.for_makers: Makers can build second screen experiences, like slides or games that use a TV and a phone as a controller. It brings big screen use to the web.

use_cases.example: You present slides on a TV while your phone shows speaker notes.
A party game shows the board on the TV and uses phones as controllers.
A music site shows lyrics on a big screen.
A teacher casts a quiz to the classroom projector.
A fitness class page shows the workout on the TV and heart rate on the phone.
A dashboard page appears on a kitchen display.

technical_bounds: No device list without a picker click
